trans.sense: interjection used to introduce a new topic
interjection used to introduce a new topic
interjection used to introduce a new topic

examples.text: So, there was this squirrel stuck in the chimney...
So, everyone wants to know – did you win the contest or not?
So, after a spell, he decided to make the best of it and shoved us into the front parlor. 'Twas a dismal sort of place, with hair wreaths, and wax fruit, and tin lambrekins, and land knows what all.
examples.ref: 1913, Joseph C[rosby] Lincoln, chapter XI, in Mr. Pratt’s Patients, New York, N.Y.; London: D[aniel] Appleton and Company, →OCLC:

glosses: Used after a pause for thought to introduce a new topic, question or story, or a new thought or question in continuation of an existing topic.

examples.text: "You park your car in front of my house every morning." — "So?"

glosses: Used as a question to ask for further explanation of something said, often rhetorically or in a dismissive or impolite manner.

examples.text: What are you doing? / So I'm just fixing this shelf.
What time does the train leave? / So it leaves at 10 o'clock.

glosses: Used as a meaningless filler word to begin a response to a question.

raw_glosses: (archaic) Be as you are; stand still; used especially to cows; also used by sailors.
